typography.description: System default sans-serif, optimized for readability for older demographics.
rules: Never truncate important labels to a single line; allow wrapping.
DO NOT use complete transparent background in header, overlays, or any surface that has content under it.
Use crisp edges and solid surfaces. Avoid complex glassmorphism that reduces readability.
Ensure logical groupings are visually separated.

header.background: Solid white or gray, never transparent.

screens.Home: Compact status card with 1 actionable primary action, ongoing Higgins concern, recent activity list.
screens.Higgins: Hub with Chat, live/recent investigations, redacted history, saved reports, Learn (New scams).
screens.Gates: Overview of 10 gate capability/status cards in plain English.
screens.Patrol: Deduplicated safety outcome history and filters.
screens.Settings: Ordinary preferences. Technical diagnostics under Settings -> Support.

motion.transitions: Subtle opacity and translation for screen changes.
motion.interactions: Clear highlight/underlay on button press. Avoid heavy animations.

accessibility.tap_targets: Minimum 48x48 points for all interactive elements.
accessibility.contrast: Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for all text against background.
accessibility.screen_reader: All images, buttons, and state indicators must have accessible labels.
accessibility.data_testid: All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a data-testid attribute.

media.icons: Use universally recognized vector icons (Lucide/Feather equivalent). Do not use emojis.
media.illustrations: Use small brand illustrations rather than full-height decorative heroes.

3d libraries: None. 2D React Native Mobile App architecture.
instructions_to_main_agent: Write all React Native components in .js files as instructed.
Record the current GitHub HEAD, then execute P2.1 through P2.6 without reopening completed baseline work (M1-M4 are complete).
Root tabs navigation order MUST be: Home, Higgins, Gates, Check It, Patrol.
All screens must have a top-right Settings action.
Translate all tech diagnostics ('DNS/VPN visibility') into plain-language actionable UI suitable for a 50+ user with no IT background.
Move raw technical diagnostics and SecureCore logic to Settings -> Support.
Ensure no 'transparent' backgrounds under content headers or modals.
Buttons must directly execute the action (no prose breadcrumbs like 'Go to Settings -> Gates').
Home screen must prioritize one actionable threat or a compact 'Apollo is checking' state.
Higgins screen must be a hub containing Chat, history, reports, and New scams, not just ordinary chat.
Check It screen contains exactly 10 explicit manual check buttons.
Include data-testid on all buttons, links, form inputs, menus, and state indicators.
Never ask for user secrets or show raw technical errors.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Do not use generic centered layouts. Maintain natural left-aligned reading flow.
Use layered design elements with z-index hierarchy but keep surfaces solid.
Never apply universal transitions in styling. Use specific interactive feedback animations.
Use modern pill-shaped or rounded-rect buttons with interaction states.
NEVER use emojis as icons; use proper vector icon libraries.
Use 2-3x more spacing to ensure breathing room and avoid cramped UI.
All interactive elements MUST have data-testid attributes.
GENERAL UI UX DESIGN GUIDELINES: Information Hierarchy: Most critical security status always at the top.
Actionability: If something is wrong, provide exactly one clear button to fix it.
Clarity over density: Use white space, avoid jargon, spell out acronyms.
No hidden menus: Keep navigation visible. 5 bottom tabs and 1 explicit top-right Settings button.
Feedback: Acknowledge user actions instantly (e.g., 'Checking Site protection...').
Plain English: Every screen and message must be understandable to a 50+ user with no IT background.
